articles.title: Rybakina makes winning start in race to number one
articles.summary: Elena Rybakina says she is "motivated" by the race to become world number one but insists her focus is on taking "one step at a time" as she got her US Open campaign off to a winning start.
body: Playing for the first time since withdrawing midway through her Cincinnati Masters quarter-final with a heel injury last month, Rybakina showed no signs of discomfort as she eased to a dominant 6-3 6-2 win over 17-year-old wildcard Thea Frodin.

The 27-year-old second seed trails Aryna Sabalenka by just 434 points in the world rankings and will become number one for the first time by reaching the semi-finals in New York – even if Sabalenka defends her title.
Regardless of her performance, Rybakina will also secure the top ranking if none of Sabalenka, Coco Gauff and Jessica Pegula lift the trophy.
"I'm definitely motivated [to become world number one]," said Rybakina, who trailed Sabalenka by more than 3,000 points in the spring before the Belarusian entered a mid-season slump.

articles.title: ‘A great feeling’: Mykhailo Mudryk seals loan move from Chelsea to Tottenham
articles.summary: Deal for Ukrainian winger has £75m purchase option. ‘I’m so excited to be reunited with De Zerbi’ Tottenham have thrown a Premier League lifeline to the forgotten Chelsea winger, Mykhailo Mudryk, signing him on loan just before the transfer deadline and challenging him to revive his career.
body: Mudryk became a €100m (£89m) player when Chelsea took him from Shakhtar Donetsk in January 2023; the deal comprised an initial €70m and €30m in add-ons. Chelsea beat Arsenal to his signature at a point when the Ukrainian was among the most in-demand players in Europe.

The move to Chelsea did not work out and Mudryk hit rock bottom when he was banned for returning an adverse reading for the banned substance, meldonium, which can increase respiratory capacity and stamina. His last competitive game for Chelsea was on 28 November 2024.

Mudryk was suspended before being given a four-year ban by the Football Association. But after an appeal to the court of arbitration for sport, he was able to resolve his case with the FA at the end of July, being cleared for an immediate return to playing. He accepted breaking anti-doping rules and agreed to a suspension that was equal to the time he had already served. The FA noted that changes have been made to the World Anti-Doping Agency’s rules on meldonium and had Mudryk’s test been conducted today then “the concentration of meldonium in the sample would not have been reported” and no adverse finding would have been recorded.

articles.title: West Ham fight off Wolves as Divine Mukasa double eases pressure on Nuno
articles.summary: It was a match between two disjointed sides, two teams trying to carve out new identities following the drop into the Championship. In the end West Ham won thanks to a bit of luck, a degree of resolve and, crucially, a sharpness in front of goal that took them away from Wolves and reduced the…
body: First half goals from Divine Mukasa and Jarrod Bowen from the penalty spot were complimented by two more in the second, as Mukasa secured his brace alongside a goal for Konstantinos Mavropanos. The defender doubled up himself too, albeit by scoring in his own end, as Wolves tried to claw their way back into contention. The visitors could also claim a decent goal from midfielder Marshall Munetsi to their tally. For all their obvious technical ability, however, Cesar Peixoto’s side lacked the hosts’ sang froid at the crucial moments and that proved the decisive factor.

Nuno’s mantra after the match was “I think we can do better”, but he was clearly grateful for the win. “We all know that it was much needed”, he said. “Looking back even on today, we have mistakes again but we’ve been much more effective in our attacking actions.”

articles.title: Man Utd fail in attempt to sign Ait-Nouri from Man City
articles.summary: Manchester United approached Manchester City in the final hours of the transfer window in an attempt to sign Algeria defender Rayan Ait-Nouri on loan
body: Manchester United failed in a shock deadline day move to sign Manchester City full-back Rayan Ait-Nouri on loan and also missed out on Leicester City's teenage midfielder Louis Page.
United have been trying to address a perceived weakness in Michael Carrick's defence for the latter part of the transfer window.

Having opted against pursuing deals for Barcelona's Alejandro Balde and Racing Santander's Jorge Salinas, and the transfer deadline less than 12 hours away, United decided to check if a deal was possible for Algeria's Ait-Nouri.
United sources say they were not interested in a permanent deal for Ait-Nouri and were told the only acceptable outcome for City would be a loan with an obligation to buy, which they rejected.

articles.title: Boss Goodwin leaves hospital but still absent from Dundee Utd role
articles.summary: Dundee United manager Jim Goodwin has been released from hospital after a health scare but it remains unclear when he will resume his duties.
body: Goodwin, 44, missed United's 4-0 Scottish Premiership win at Kilmarnock on Saturday after taking ill and being admitted to hospital last Thursday.
Assistant Lee Sharp took the team at Rugby Park, and will do so again for United's midweek trip to play Motherwell amid the Irishman's continued absence.
"He is out of hospital, he is back home recovering," Sharp said of Goodwin. "He is waiting on direction from the doctors etc to where he goes from there."
Asked if there was any indication when Goodwin would return, Sharp replied: "No. He would be back just now if he was allowed. We are in constant dialogue so he will let me know as soon as."

articles.title: Bayern Munich won’t deploy ‘goalkeeper by competition’ strategy
articles.summary: Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany has heard the theories that the squad could use a “goalkeeper by competition” strategy, but the boss does not want anyone to think that will be the case for his team during the 2026/27 season.
body: “I dismiss the idea of having a dedicated cup or Champions League goalkeeper. We’re looking at the fixture list; it’s about seeing what’s best – also for Manuel Neuer and giving Jonas a chance to shine. I did that once in my first year as head coach, and it was a mistake,” said Kompany (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ). “Jonas Urbig will start in goal tomorrow. Over the course of the season, it will be the same as last term. We’ve already put an incredible amount of trust in Jonas. He’s played in many important matches, such as the cup final. These are milestones that show he can perform in big games.”

For the betterment of the squad — and also the health of Neuer and the development of Urbig — Kompany will manage the workload balance as he sees fit and base it on how he assesses each player, not on what competition a game is in.

articles.summary: No Julian Alvarez to Arsenal. He joins Morgan Rogers and Vinicius Junior in not moving to the Premier League champions this summer. And Mikel Arteta has missed out on the star attacker he wanted.
body: Arsenal failed to bring in an elite attacker in the transfer window after going for Julian Alvarez, Vinicius Junior and Morgan Rogers; after selling four first-team forwards, are Arsenal short in attack this season - and has it opened up the title race?

After a summer-long transfer saga, Alvarez will now stay at Atletico Madrid after he tried to force through a move to Spanish rivals Barcelona, with Arsenal unsuccessful in convincing him to move back to the Premier League while waiting in the wings.

Speaking after the Champions League final defeat to Paris Saint-Germain, Arteta demanded Arsenal be "ambitious" and "fast" in the transfer market. The jury is very much out about whether Arsenal delivered on those two ambitions.

Arsenal started the summer with Rogers as their No 1 forward target. He went to Chelsea in a £117m, which Arsenal thought was too steep. They moved to an ambitious Vinicius Junior approach - but he stayed at Real Madrid.

articles.summary: When you look around the NFL landscape on September 1st, it’s easy to get tunnel vision and focus only on the Chicago Bears. You might be worried about the health of the Bears’ secondary, you might be worried about the left tackle position, but you aren’t worried about the quarterback.
body: So when we look around the rest of the league, we should pause and say, “Thank you, Caleb Williams.”

articles.summary: There is a story about Brooke Norton-Cuffy's time as a teenager on loan at Lincoln City under Michael Appleton that highlights his maturity. “It is one that Michael and I still speak about,” Rich O’Donnell, then Lincoln’s assistant coach, tells Sky Sports.
body: With Brooke Norton-Cuffy making a Transfer Deadline Day move to Hull from Genoa, Adam Bate speaks to the England Under-21 international's former coaches at Lincoln and Rotherham to find out why playing early was so important for his development...

It involved John Marquis, a big, strong centre-forward with vast experience in English football's lower leagues and a dominant figure in any dressing room. Given that he was over a decade older than the young Norton-Cuffy, keeping quiet was the easy option.

"We had taken John on loan from Portsmouth to Lincoln from January until the end of the season. In an analysis meeting after a game, John, who is quite a big character, was vocal, discussing things that we have to defend better and how we should not concede.

"Brooke, as an 18-year-old lad, just said, 'I agree John and what you are saying is right. However, if you had scored the two opportunities you had, it would not matter about us defending.' It was non-confrontational, just a guy speaking about football and how it is."
